## Natural history notes

A small geometrid moth characterized by chocolate-brown to grayish-brown wings with angular outer edges, fine wavy crosslines, and bark-like mottling that helps it blend into tree trunks and woody stems. In Florida, it is found in pine flatwoods, sandhills, open pine woodlands, forest edges, and other habitats where southern pines occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on pine foliage, especially longleaf pine and slash pine, helping move pine needles into the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
